Check out our strategy here: https://lnkd.in/gmxxJfax","url":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/maritime-new-zealand_alongside-our-safer-boating-partners-we-activity-7475050026231033856-p659"},{"@context":"http://schema.org","@type":"DiscussionForumPosting","author":{"@type":"Organization","name":"Maritime New Zealand","url":"https://nz.linkedin.com/company/maritime-new-zealand"},"datePublished":"2026-06-22T03:13:54.119Z","mainEntityOfPage":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/maritime-new-zealand_our-rescue-coordination-centre-has-played-activity-7474660913002881024-aL6l","text":"Our Rescue Coordination Centre has played a key role in finding a lost Cook Islands fisherman – more than a week after going missing. 

The man left to go fishing on 11 June from Pukapuka Island, he did not return. Local authorities undertook an initial search. 

RCCNZ Operation’s Manager, Mike Clulow says we were asked to assist on Wednesday 17 June. At the request of RCCNZ the New Zealand Defence Force deployed a Royal New Zealand Airforce P-8A Poseidon to undertake a search. 

“Following an extensive search, he was spotted alive by the crew of a Royal New Zealand Air Force (RNZAF) P-8A Poseidon on Friday morning (19 July),” he says. 

When the plane flew overhead, he was waving a paddle. 

He was picked up by a Taiwanese fishing vessel on Friday evening (19 July). We want to thank RCC Taipei which assisted by putting us in contact with the fishing vessel. 

“This is a brilliant result, being able to bring this man safely back to shore after more than a week. 

“His boat has drifted more than 200 nautical miles from Pukapuka Island. It is currently about 150 nautical miles north of Apia (Samoa),” Mike says. 

“The RCCNZ would like to acknowledge support of the New Zealand Defence Force’s support in this operation, RCC Taipei and the local authorities and operators who have assisted our efforts in locating the missing man,” Mike Clulow says.

","url":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/maritime-new-zealand_its-volunteer-week-and-were-saying-activity-7473525026328059904-FVzN"},{"@context":"http://schema.org","@type":"DiscussionForumPosting","author":{"@type":"Organization","name":"Maritime New Zealand","url":"https://nz.linkedin.com/company/maritime-new-zealand"},"datePublished":"2026-06-17T22:00:05.234Z","mainEntityOfPage":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/maritime-new-zealand_be-aware-of-the-dangers-that-equipment-activity-7473132387472781313-0cB5","text":"⚠️ Be aware of the dangers that equipment that produces carbon monoxide can cause

In the winter of 2025, two men stayed overnight on their boat in a Southland lake. 

They used a diesel heater to heat the cabin and ran a petrol generator on deck to power satellite broadband. 

The next day they were reported overdue. One man died and the second was dangerously sick but was able to be stabilised.

The diesel heater created negative pressure in the cabin and drew carbon monoxide from the petrol generator inside. 

Testing showed that carbon monoxide reached fatal levels in just 3.5 hours.

⚓ Lessons for boaties:
❗Remember that any equipment that generates or might generate carbon monoxide can be a risk.
⏰ Minimise the risk of carbon monoxide buildup by ventilating your cabin well and installing a carbon monoxide detector.

See the full investigation insight for more information: https://lnkd.in/gu_38tfJ","url":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/maritime-new-zealand_be-aware-of-the-dangers-that-equipment-activity-7473132387472781313-0cB5"},{"@context":"http://schema.org","@type":"DiscussionForumPosting","author":{"@type":"Organization","name":"Maritime New Zealand","url":"https://nz.linkedin.com/company/maritime-new-zealand"},"datePublished":"2026-06-05T21:00:04.413Z","mainEntityOfPage":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/maritime-new-zealand_from-all-of-us-at-maritime-new-zealand-we-activity-7468768630135177216-4jSD","text":"From all of us at Maritime New Zealand, we would like to congratulate a valued member of our extended community who has been made a Member of the New Zealand Order of Merit.

Captain Alex van Wijngaarden received this honour in the King’s Birthday Honours, recognising more than 40 years of service to the maritime industry.

Captain van Wijngaarden has made a significant contribution to the wider maritime sector, particularly as both a responder and a trainer.

Since 1996, he has served as one of our National On Scene Commanders and has played a key role in leading responses to several major maritime incidents, including the Rena (2011) and Jody F Millennium oil spill (2002), the sinking and subsequent oil spill of Sea Fresh 1 in 2000, and the grounding of Dong Won 529 in 1998.

In addition to his operational work, Captain van Wijngaarden has played an important role in training maritime responders. Over the course of his career, it is estimated that he has helped train hundreds of maritime responders, particularly in leadership roles. 

Long-time maritime response colleague Mick Courtnell said that this recognition reflects the time, effort, and dedication Alex has given to maritime response both nationally and in Marlborough.

“Alex’s contribution through training responders and sharing his knowledge will have a lasting impact on the sector and our people at Maritime NZ.

“He is a true legend of our industry,” Mick said.

    <p class="attributed-text-segment-list__content text-color-text !text-sm whitespace-pre-wrap break-words
        " dir="ltr" data-test-id="main-feed-activity-card__commentary">Two climbers were brought safely to warmth and comfort after getting into difficulty on Mount Aspiring earlier this week. 

The pair became stuck on the North West ridge on Tuesday night and activated their personal locator beacon. The Rescue Coordination Centre received the alert shortly before 8.30pm that evening. 

An overnight rescue was coordinated with two rescue helicopters, supported by a <a class="link" href="https://nz.linkedin.com/company/land-search-and-rescue-new-zealand?trk=organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" target="_self" data-tracking-control-name="organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" data-tracking-will-navigate>Land Search and Rescue New Zealand</a> Alpine Cliff Rescue team. The rescue operation took most of the night and was technically challenging due to the terrain and weather conditions. 

The climbers were eventually successfully uplifted up from the mountain and taken to Queenstown for medical assessment early on Wednesday morning. 

Maritime New Zealand’s Rescue Coordination Centre want to thank all the responders who worked through the night to get the climbers back to safety. 

Carrying a distress beacon made a big difference in ensuring the climbers were able to get assistance when they needed it.</p>

        " dir="ltr" data-test-id="main-feed-activity-card__commentary">Our Rescue Coordination Centre has played a key role in finding a lost Cook Islands fisherman – more than a week after going missing. 

The man left to go fishing on 11 June from Pukapuka Island, he did not return. Local authorities undertook an initial search. 

RCCNZ Operation’s Manager, Mike Clulow says we were asked to assist on Wednesday 17 June. At the request of RCCNZ the <a class="link" href="https://nz.linkedin.com/company/new-zealand-defence-force?trk=organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" target="_self" data-tracking-control-name="organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" data-tracking-will-navigate>New Zealand Defence Force</a> deployed a Royal New Zealand Airforce P-8A Poseidon to undertake a search. 

“Following an extensive search, he was spotted alive by the crew of a Royal New Zealand Air Force (RNZAF) P-8A Poseidon on Friday morning (19 July),” he says. 

When the plane flew overhead, he was waving a paddle. 

He was picked up by a Taiwanese fishing vessel on Friday evening (19 July). We want to thank RCC Taipei which assisted by putting us in contact with the fishing vessel. 

“This is a brilliant result, being able to bring this man safely back to shore after more than a week. 

“His boat has drifted more than 200 nautical miles from Pukapuka Island. It is currently about 150 nautical miles north of Apia (Samoa),” Mike says. 

“The RCCNZ would like to acknowledge support of the New Zealand Defence Force’s support in this operation, RCC Taipei and the local authorities and operators who have assisted our efforts in locating the missing man,” Mike Clulow says. 

Photo credit: New Zealand Defence Force. Taken from the P-8A as it flew overhead.</p>

        " dir="ltr" data-test-id="main-feed-activity-card__commentary">⚠️ Be aware of the dangers that equipment that produces carbon monoxide can cause

In the winter of 2025, two men stayed overnight on their boat in a Southland lake. 

They used a diesel heater to heat the cabin and ran a petrol generator on deck to power satellite broadband. 

The next day they were reported overdue. One man died and the second was dangerously sick but was able to be stabilised.

The diesel heater created negative pressure in the cabin and drew carbon monoxide from the petrol generator inside. 

Testing showed that carbon monoxide reached fatal levels in just 3.5 hours.

⚓ Lessons for boaties:
❗Remember that any equipment that generates or might generate carbon monoxide can be a risk.
⏰ Minimise the risk of carbon monoxide buildup by ventilating your cabin well and installing a carbon monoxide detector.

Captain Alex van Wijngaarden received this honour in the King’s Birthday Honours, recognising more than 40 years of service to the maritime industry.

Captain van Wijngaarden has made a significant contribution to the wider maritime sector, particularly as both a responder and a trainer.

Since 1996, he has served as one of our National On Scene Commanders and has played a key role in leading responses to several major maritime incidents, including the Rena (2011) and Jody F Millennium oil spill (2002), the sinking and subsequent oil spill of Sea Fresh 1 in 2000, and the grounding of Dong Won 529 in 1998.

In addition to his operational work, Captain van Wijngaarden has played an important role in training maritime responders. Over the course of his career, it is estimated that he has helped train hundreds of maritime responders, particularly in leadership roles. 

Long-time maritime response colleague Mick Courtnell said that this recognition reflects the time, effort, and dedication Alex has given to maritime response both nationally and in Marlborough.

“Alex’s contribution through training responders and sharing his knowledge will have a lasting impact on the sector and our people at Maritime NZ.

“He is a true legend of our industry,” Mick said.
